sources.prices: finance-chart-daily.json — this page's own price file

method.leaderboard: Members ranked by total disclosed volume over the trailing 12 months of filings, each trade counted at the midpoint of its disclosed range (an estimate — trades themselves are always shown as ranges); ties broken by trade count.
method.performance: For each disclosed buy, the underlying stock's return from the trade date to the latest close in this page's price file, weighted by range midpoint. Only buys in stocks the price file covers are graded; the covered count is shown with every figure.
method.clusters: A ticker appears when at least 3 different members bought it within one rolling 45-day window of trade dates; each cluster shows its strongest such window from the trailing 12 months of filings, with the window's dates. Disclosure lag means the most recent weeks are always incompletely filed, so clusters are not filtered to 'recent' ones.
method.curves: A reconstruction from the disclosed trades, not the member's real account: each covered buy opens a position sized at its range midpoint at the trade date's close in this page's price file; sells close the oldest positions first; sales of positions opened before the window are left out, as are trades in stocks the price file does not cover. Indexed to 100 at the window's start, beside the S&P 500 over the same weeks.
method.late: The STOCK Act gives a member 45 days from a trade to disclose it. A filing that took longer is flagged with the number of days past the deadline — the dates themselves, stated plainly.
method.committees: A trade is marked when a committee the member sits on oversees the sector the traded stock belongs to — Armed Services and defense, Financial Services and banks, Energy and Commerce and energy, and the like, under a short explicit map. Appropriations is left out: it funds everything, so a match there would say nothing. The mark is jurisdiction context only; it claims nothing about why a trade happened.
